co-bars.1.t0.name: co-bars.1.t0.eleven_v3
co-bars.1.t0.text: a lower rate cuts the monthly payment.

co-bill.1.t0.name: co-bill.1.t0.eleven_v3
co-bill.1.t0.text: But the refinance has a price, and the savings must repay it first.

co-question.1.t0.name: co-question.1.t0.eleven_v3
co-question.1.t0.text: So how far do raids have to fall before a refinance pays for itself?

a1-lab.1.t0.name: a1-lab.1.t0.eleven_v3
a1-lab.1.t0.text: This is a lab for money decisions. We run the numbers on public data and show every assumption.

a1-scope.1.t0.name: a1-scope.1.t0.eleven_v3
a1-scope.1.t0.text: U .S. only. The rates here are history, not a forecast.

a1-rehook.1.t0.name: a1-rehook.1.t0.eleven_v3
a1-rehook.1.t0.text: By the end, you will see the exact rate drop that repays a typical refinance within 36 months, and how every rate drop since 1971 actually played out.

a1-rates.1.t0.name: a1-rates.1.t0.eleven_v3
a1-rates.1.t0.text: Here's the rate itself, the weekly average for a 30 -year fixed mortgage from Freddie Mac's survey.

a1-drops.1.t0.name: a1-drops.1.t0.eleven_v3
a1-drops.1.t0.text: Every fall in that line is a moment when homeowners asked the same question.

a1-q.1.t0.name: a1-q.1.t0.eleven_v3
a1-q.1.t0.text: First question, then what does a refinance actually cost?

a1-hmda.1.t0.name: a1-hmda.1.t0.eleven_v3
a1-hmda.1.t0.text: Lenders report it for every loan they make, under the Home Mortgage Disclosure Act, as total loan costs.

a1-terms.1.t0.name: a1-terms.1.t0.eleven_v3
a1-terms.1.t0.text: Those are the closing costs, origination charges, discount points, the appraisal, title insurance, and the rest.

a1-points.1.t0.name: a1-points.1.t0.eleven_v3
a1-points.1.t0.text: Discount points are optional. Paying more at closing buys a lower rate. So part of that bill is a choice.

a1-cashout.1.t0.name: a1-cashout.1.t0.eleven_v3
a1-cashout.1.t0.text: cash out refinances, which also take equity out of the house, cost more. A median of $8 ,655. This film keeps to refinances that change only the rate and the term.

a1-count.1.t0.name: a1-count.1.t0.eleven_v3
a1-count.1.t0.text: In 2025, lenders reported 488 ,241 of those into 30 -year first mortgages.

a1-median.1.t0.name: a1-median.1.t0.eleven_v3
a1-median.1.t0.text: In nominal dollars, the median one cost $5 ,124.

a1-spread.1.t0.name: a1-spread.1.t0.eleven_v3
a1-spread.1.t0.text: The middle half paid between $3 ,443 and $8 ,270.

a1-boom.1.t0.name: a1-boom.1.t0.eleven_v3
a1-boom.1.t0.text: The count follows the rate. In 2021, near the bottom, lenders reported 3 ,089 ,298 of them.

a1-boomcost.1.t0.name: a1-boomcost.1.t0.eleven_v3
a1-boomcost.1.t0.text: Their median bill that year was $3 ,406.

a1-turn.1.t0.name: a1-turn.1.t0.eleven_v3
a1-turn.1.t0.text: But the dollar figure hides the real pattern. The bill barely grows with the size of the loan.

a1-small.1.t0.name: a1-small.1.t0.eleven_v3
a1-small.1.t0.text: On loans under $150 ,000, the median cost was 3 .4 % of the amount borrowed.

a1-big.1.t0.name: a1-big.1.t0.eleven_v3
a1-big.1.t0.text: On loans of $750 ,000 and more, it was 0 .5%.

a1-keep.1.t0.name: a1-keep.1.t0.eleven_v3
a1-keep.1.t0.text: So the same cut in rate repays a large loan faster than a small one. Keep that in mind, it comes back.

a1-rule.1.t0.name: a1-rule.1.t0.eleven_v3
a1-rule.1.t0.text: Paying the bill back is simple division. The closing costs divided by the drop in the monthly payment.

a1-payoff.1.t0.name: a1-payoff.1.t0.eleven_v3
a1-payoff.1.t0.text: The answer is the break -even, the month when the savings have covered the bill.

a1-after.1.t0.name: a1-after.1.t0.eleven_v3
a1-after.1.t0.text: Before that month, the refinance is still in the red. After it, every payment is money kept.

a2-q.1.t0.name: a2-q.1.t0.eleven_v3
a2-q.1.t0.text: Now the main question, how big does the drop have to be?

a2-loan.1.t0.name: a2-loan.1.t0.eleven_v3
a2-loan.1.t0.text: Take the median refinance, a balance of $375 ,000 and $5 ,124 to close.

a2-old.1.t0.name: a2-old.1.t0.eleven_v3
a2-old.1.t0.text: Say the old loan carries 7 .62%. The average rate in the month, the last big drop again, October, 2023.

a2-s025.1.t0.name: a2-s025.1.t0.eleven_v3
a2-s025.1.t0.text: cut the rate by 0 .25 points, and the payment falls by $64 a month.

a2-be025.1.t0.name: a2-be025.1.t0.eleven_v3
a2-be025.1.t0.text: At that pace, the bill takes 80 months to come back.

a2-s05.1.t0.name: a2-s05.1.t0.eleven_v3
a2-s05.1.t0.text: Double the cut to 0 .5 points and the payment falls by $128 a month.

a2-s10.1.t0.name: a2-s10.1.t0.eleven_v3
a2-s10.1.t0.text: A cut of one point saves $253 a month.

a2-be10.1.t0.name: a2-be10.1.t0.eleven_v3
a2-be10.1.t0.text: That pays back the bill in 21 months.

a2-s20.1.t0.name: a2-s20.1.t0.eleven_v3
a2-s20.1.t0.text: Two points pay back in 11 months. Well, inside a year.

a2-curve.1.t0.name: a2-curve.1.t0.eleven_v3
a2-curve.1.t0.text: Look at the shape of that curve. It is not a straight line.

a2-cliff.1.t0.name: a2-cliff.1.t0.eleven_v3
a2-cliff.1.t0.text: Below 0 .5 points it climbs steeply. Each smaller cut adds years, not months.

a2-thumb.1.t0.name: a2-thumb.1.t0.eleven_v3
a2-thumb.1.t0.text: That is where the common rule of thumb about a full point comes from. For this loan, one point pays back in 21 months, 0 .5 points in 41.

a2-turn.1.t0.name: a2-turn.1.t0.eleven_v3
a2-turn.1.t0.text: But remember the pattern in the costs and move the same question to a different loan.

a2-mid.1.t0.name: a2-mid.1.t0.eleven_v3
a2-mid.1.t0.text: To break even within 36 months, the median loan needs a cut of 0 .56 points.

a2-small.1.t0.name: a2-small.1.t0.eleven_v3
a2-small.1.t0.text: A loan under $150 ,000 needs 1 .32 points because its bill is a bigger share of the balance.

a2-big.1.t0.name: a2-big.1.t0.eleven_v3
a2-big.1.t0.text: A loan of $750 ,000 or more needs only 0 .2.

a2-hold60.1.t0.name: a2-hold60.1.t0.eleven_v3
a2-hold60.1.t0.text: give the median loan 60 months instead, and 0 .33 points is enough.

a2-hold84.1.t0.name: a2-hold84.1.t0.eleven_v3
a2-hold84.1.t0.text: give it 84 months, and it needs 0 .24.

a2-flip.1.t0.name: a2-flip.1.t0.eleven_v3
a2-flip.1.t0.text: Read each of those as a flip point. Below it, the bill outlasts the stay. Above it, the savings win.

a2-payoff.1.t0.name: a2-payoff.1.t0.eleven_v3
a2-payoff.1.t0.text: So there is no single threshold. The drop that pays back depends on two things, how big the loan is and how long it is kept.

a2-hold.1.t0.name: a2-hold.1.t0.eleven_v3
a2-hold.1.t0.text: and how long it is kept is the one number no dataset can supply.

a2-reset.1.t0.name: a2-reset.1.t0.eleven_v3
a2-reset.1.t0.text: One more cost hides inside the new loan. It starts a fresh 30 years, so the last payment moves further away, even when each payment is smaller.

a2-reset2.1.t0.name: a2-reset2.1.t0.eleven_v3
a2-reset2.1.t0.text: The simple division ignores that. It answers only the first question. When do the savings cover the bill?

a3-q.1.t0.name: a3-q.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-q.1.t0.text: The division assumes the new rate is the last one. What happened in the real drops?

a3-all.1.t0.name: a3-all.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-all.1.t0.text: We found every fall of at least one point in the 30 -year rate since 1971, 13 of them.

a3-rules.1.t0.name: a3-rules.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-rules.1.t0.text: In each, a borrower who took a loan at the peak refinances in the first month, the rate is one point lower.

a3-costs.1.t0.name: a3-costs.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-costs.1.t0.text: closing costs use the median share for that year. Before 2018, lenders did not report them, so a fixed share is used and marked illustrative.

a3-80s.1.t0.name: a3-80s.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-80s.1.t0.text: The steepest falls came in the early 1980s.

a3-81.1.t0.name: a3-81.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-81.1.t0.text: After the peak of 1981, the first cut of one point came two months later.

a3-81be.1.t0.name: a3-81be.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-81be.1.t0.text: It paid back in 13 months, but the slide went on, and the next point came nine months after the refinance.

a3-short.1.t0.name: a3-short.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-short.1.t0.text: Some drops were brief. The fall that began in 1987 lasted four months and the refinance came at its very bottom.

a3-06.1.t0.name: a3-06.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-06.1.t0.text: The drop that began in 2006 was slower, the refinance came in January 2008, and it had paid for itself before the next point arrived.

a3-range.1.t0.name: a3-range.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-range.1.t0.text: At a cut of one point, break -even took between 10 and 21 months across all 13 drops.

a3-turn.1.t0.name: a3-turn.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-turn.1.t0.text: But in five of them, the rate kept falling. Another drop of one point before the first refinance had paid for itself.

a3-twice.1.t0.name: a3-twice.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-twice.1.t0.text: Those borrowers met the same question twice, and a second refinance starts a new clock with a new bill.

a3-example.1.t0.name: a3-example.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-example.1.t0.text: In the drop that began in November 2018, the refinance came in June 2019.

a3-example2.1.t0.name: a3-example2.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-example2.1.t0.text: It needed 18 months to break even. And the next drop of one point came only 17 months later.

a3-quiet.1.t0.name: a3-quiet.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-quiet.1.t0.text: In the other eight, the first refinance was the one that mattered.

a3-23.1.t0.name: a3-23.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-23.1.t0.text: The latest drop began in October, 2023. The cut of one point arrived in August, 2024.

a3-23be.1.t0.name: a3-23be.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-23be.1.t0.text: At that year's median cost, it paid back in 21 months.

a3-answer.1.t0.name: a3-answer.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-answer.1.t0.text: So, how far do rates have to fall before a refinance pays for itself?

a3-answer2.1.t0.name: a3-answer2.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-answer2.1.t0.text: For the median loan and median costs, a cut that repays it within 36 months is 0 .56 points.

a3-answer3.1.t0.name: a3-answer3.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-answer3.1.t0.text: Half as much patience asks for more. To pay back in 21 months takes one point.

a3-limit.1.t0.name: a3-limit.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-limit.1.t0.text: That answer has limits. It counts payment savings only, no taxes, no return on the cash, and a new 30 -year loan restarts the clock on owning the house outright.

a3-median.1.t0.name: a3-median.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-median.1.t0.text: It uses medians. Half of borrowers paid more than $5 ,124, and an offered rate can differ from the survey average.

a3-history.1.t0.name: a3-history.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-history.1.t0.text: And it is history, not a forecast. Nothing here says where rates go next.

a3-close.1.t0.name: a3-close.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-close.1.t0.text: What history does show is the shape of the trade. A known bill upfront against savings that arrive one month at a time for as long as the loan lasts.

m-rates.1.t0.name: m-rates.1.t0.eleven_v3
m-rates.1.t0.text: method. Rates are Freddie Mac's weekly survey via Fred, checked against the optimal blue index since 2017.

m-drops.1.t0.name: m-drops.1.t0.eleven_v3
m-drops.1.t0.text: A drop counts when the monthly average falls at least one point from a peak before rising one point from its low.

m-costs.1.t0.name: m-costs.1.t0.eleven_v3
m-costs.1.t0.text: Costs are HMDA. Loan level data from 2018 to 2025 originated refinances, first lien, 30 year term.

m-assume.1.t0.name: m-assume.1.t0.eleven_v3
m-assume.1.t0.text: Closing costs are paid in cash, with no taxes and no discounting. Every figure and formula is listed in the description.

o-recap.1.t0.name: o-recap.1.t0.eleven_v3
o-recap.1.t0.text: A small cut needs a long stay, a large loan needs a smaller cut, and a falling rate can make the first refinance too early.

o-close.1.t0.name: o-close.1.t0.eleven_v3
o-close.1.t0.text: The break -even is simple division. The hard part is the number only the borrower knows. How long the loan will be kept.

o-bill.1.t0.name: o-bill.1.t0.eleven_v3
o-bill.1.t0.text: The bill is known the day the loan closes. The savings arrive one month at a time.

o-sources.1.t0.name: o-sources.1.t0.eleven_v3
o-sources.1.t0.text: The sources are linked in the description, and the next decision is already on the bench.
